paragraphs.text: Eleven stainless steel plaques on a backboard, in a glazed stainless steel frame, hang in Burn Methodist Chapel. They record 219 aircrew of 578 Squadron killed, with 79 taken prisoner and 45 aircraft lost. The memorial was designed by the architect Hugh Cawdron, cost 750 pounds, and was unveiled and dedicated on 16 May 1999 by Rev Owain Williams. The 578 Burn Association presented it to the people of Burn. IWM names Burn Village Council as custodian. A separate roadside stone to the squadron stands on the A19 opposite the Wheatsheaf Inn.

retractions.reason: Our record says Burn Village Council erected it. IWM says the 578 Burn Association presented the memorial to the people of Burn (designer Hugh Cawdron); Burn Village Council is named as custodian, not erector. Replaced by the IWM wording.

notes: CUSTODIAN: Burn Village Council, per IWM (institutional). IWM says 'Burn Village Council is the custodian' and gives no separate maintenance arrangement. Not corroborated by a second publisher, and I did not find the council's own website or a contact, so a human should confirm with the council (also check whether it is a parish council, since a web snippet mentions 'Burn Parish Council' for the Snowbirds event). The 'erected by Burn Village Council' claim in our record is wrong per IWM: the 578 Burn Association presented it. The chapel is a Methodist church in the Goole and Selby circuit; the circuit page does not mention the memorial and I did not establish whether the chapel trustees share custody. A DIFFERENT 578 Sqn memorial (roadside stone on A19, WMO/243643) also exists, with no custodian listed; do not confuse. IWM page lists no names. Our narrative's 'now farmland' etc. and the 'Farnsfield Halifax MZ519' aside are unchecked here. Our dedication date 1999-05-16 matches IWM.
